_note: Golden pin targets for the Sdk 2.3.2 -> 2.4.0 cascade. This is the wire shape of a pin cascade: there is no DTO or endpoint, so the 'fields' every consumer must cite verbatim are the version strings and pin counts below. A child change that writes 'bump to latest' instead of citing these values verbatim is a blocking finding in the boundary reconciliation matrix, exactly as a paraphrased DTO field name would be.

sdkBaseline.apiChange: none — 2.4.0 is a pure dependency-bump release (Verbara.Sdk CHANGELOG.md, '### Changed — Dependency bumps')

raisedTransitiveFloors._source: git show v2.4.0:Directory.Packages.props in Verbara.Sdk — these are the floors the PUBLISHED 2.4.0 packages declare, not Sdk main
raisedTransitiveFloors._nu1605Set: Only Microsoft.Extensions.* collides: both consumers pin it DIRECTLY at 10.0.9, below the 10.0.10 floor. NATS.Client.Core and OpenTelemetry are pinned directly by NEITHER consumer and arrive purely transitively.

packageVersion._why: release.yml extracts this element and tags off it; merging pin changes WITHOUT bumping it is a silent no-op release (Verbara.Sdk.Pro openspec/config.yaml). Patch level follows the two prior cascade precedents: v2.8.1-pro (Sdk 2.3.0) and 2.11.1-pro (Sdk 2.3.2).

outOfScope.reason: Test-only, different servicing track. ADR-0040 D4: scope is declared, not inferred — a blanket Microsoft.Extensions.* rewrite that sweeps this in is a defect.

Deliberately left on its own prerelease cadence by Sdk 2.4.0. Verbara.Sdk.Pro.OpenTelemetry suppresses NU5104 for it (src/Verbara.Sdk.Pro.OpenTelemetry/*.csproj:6-10) — watch that suppression, do not remove it.

prefixHazards: 'Verbara.Sdk.' also matches 'Verbara.Sdk.Pro.' in Verbara.Platform/Directory.Packages.props. Any rewrite must anchor on Verbara.Sdk. NOT followed by Pro. — the two families move to DIFFERENT versions in this cascade (2.4.0 vs 2.13.1-pro).
'Microsoft.Extensions.*' also matches Microsoft.Extensions.TimeProvider.Testing, which is out of scope in both repos.

sourceExposure._rule: ADR-0040 D5 — a major in the transitive closure is a review item scoped by real source exposure.

NATS.Client.Core 3.x.Verbara.Sdk.Pro: ZERO. Repo-wide grep for NATS/Nats in src/ + tests/ returns 3 hits, all string literals in tests/Verbara.Sdk.Pro.Governance.Tests (ProjectGraph.cs:20 provider-suffix list, LayeringGuardTests.cs:8,120). No *.Nats project, no NATS.Client.* reference, no using NATS.
NATS.Client.Core 3.x.Verbara.Platform: ZERO. grep -rn -i nats src/ returns zero hits. All NATS mentions are docs/history; Platform's realtime transport is SignalR + StackExchange.Redis. docker/docker-compose.coturn.yml:21 'NATs' is NAT traversal, a false positive.
NATS.Client.Core 3.x._conclusion: NATS 3.x cannot break either consumer at source level. Exposure reduces to (a) restore resolution and (b) AOT publish behaviour of the new NATS assembly inside the Api publish closure — only reachable at all via Verbara.Sdk.Push.Nats, which neither consumer references. Both are covered by existing required CI gates.
